# RivalIQ — NBA Strategy Assistant

**RAG + LLM generation + Reinforcement Learning, combined into one system, entirely on free APIs**: retrieval-grounded scouting reports, generated by Groq's free-tier Llama 3.3 70B, paired with a reinforcement-learning agent that learns clutch-time play-calling strategy — calibrated to real, live NBA data from balldontlie's free tier.

**[Live demo](#) — add your deployed Hugging Face Spaces / Render link here**

## Why this project

Most fresher AI/ML portfolios show either a chatbot wrapper or a research notebook. This project demonstrates the full stack of what a production applied-AI role actually needs:

- **Data engineering**: a real API client with caching and rate-limit handling, plus a from-scratch analytics layer deriving team performance metrics from raw game data (the free API tier doesn't provide pre-built stats — so this project computes them)
- **Retrieval-augmented generation**: structured + semantic retrieval over derived team data, with an LLM generation layer that is prompted and evaluated to stay strictly grounded in retrieved facts
- **Reinforcement learning**: a genuine sequential decision problem (not a bandit) where a Q-learning agent learns state-dependent clutch-time strategy, benchmarked against baselines with a measured, plotted improvement
- **Evaluation discipline**: a deterministic RAG faithfulness checker (catches hallucinated numbers) and an RL learning curve vs. multiple baselines — not just a demo that "looks like it works"

**One-line pitch:** *An NBA strategy assistant where a reinforcement-learning agent learns optimal clutch-time play-calling from a simulation calibrated to real team data, paired with a retrieval-grounded LLM scouting report — combining my RL research background with production LLM engineering.*

## Project structure

```
rivaliq/
├── app.py                       # Streamlit UI tying every layer together
├── data/
│   ├── client.py                  # balldontlie API client (cached, rate-limited)
│   └── analytics.py                # derives team stats from raw game results
├── rag/
│   ├── notes.py                    # stats -> retrievable scouting-note text
│   ├── retriever.py                 # exact team lookup + TF-IDF semantic search
│   └── generator.py                 # Groq (free, default) / Claude (paid) grounded report generation
├── rl/
│   ├── environment.py               # clutch-possession MDP (the core sim)
│   ├── team_params.py               # maps real stats -> RL environment skill params
│   └── agent.py                     # tabular Q-learning agent + training loop
├── genai/
│   └── visuals.py                   # radar chart + learning-curve chart generation
├── eval/
│   ├── faithfulness.py               # RAG faithfulness scorer
│   └── run_eval.py                    # full pipeline eval across several matchups
├── cache/                        # cached API responses (gitignored)
└── requirements.txt
```

## Setup (local, macOS)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/rivaliq.git
cd rivaliq
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env
streamlit run app.py
```

Everything runs on free APIs by default - no credit card needed for either external service:

### 1. Groq (free) — report generation

1. Sign up at [console.groq.com](https://console.groq.com/keys) (no credit card).
2. Create an API key (starts with `gsk_...`).
3. Paste it into `.env` as `GROQ_API_KEY=...`, or into the sidebar when the app is running.

The app defaults to `provider="groq"` with `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` on Groq's free tier. Prefer Claude instead? Get a key at [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com/settings/keys) (pay-as-you-go, no ongoing free tier), then switch **Report-generation provider** to "Anthropic (paid)" in the sidebar, or pass `provider="anthropic"` to `ScoutingReportGenerator(...)` / `--provider anthropic` to `eval/run_eval.py`.

### 2. balldontlie (free) — NBA data

1. Sign up at [app.balldontlie.io](https://app.balldontlie.io) (no credit card).
2. Copy your API key from the dashboard.
3. Paste it into `.env` as `BALLDONTLIE_API_KEY=...`, or into the sidebar.

Note: balldontlie's free tier is rate-limited to 5 requests/minute and covers Teams, Players, and Games (the endpoints this project uses) - no paid tier needed. The client caches every response to disk (`cache/`) so repeated runs during development don't burn the limit - delete `cache/*.json` if you want fresh data.

## Running the full evaluation

```bash
export GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_...
export BALLDONTLIE_API_KEY=...
python eval/run_eval.py

# Or benchmark the report-generation step against Claude instead:
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
python eval/run_eval.py --provider anthropic
```

This runs the complete pipeline (real data → RAG report → faithfulness score → RL training → baseline comparison → charts) for a configurable list of matchups (edit `MATCHUPS` in `eval/run_eval.py`), and writes results to `eval/results.json` plus charts to `eval/charts/`.

## Results worth highlighting

On the BOS vs. LAL matchup (2024 season sample), the RL agent trained for 8,000 episodes reached a **~74% win rate** in the simulated clutch scenario, versus **~66-67% for naive fixed strategies** ("always shoot 2s"/"always shoot 3s") and **~40% for a random policy**. More interestingly, the *learned policy is basketball-intuitive*, not just numerically better:
- When **leading late** with few possessions left, the agent learns to **stall** (deny the opponent extra possessions) — a real defensive strategy concept.
- When **trailing late**, the agent learns to use the **foul strategy** (sacrifice a possession's scoring to manufacture an extra chance to catch up) — exactly what real teams do in end-game situations.

This is the strongest piece to walk through in an interview: the agent wasn't told these are good strategies — it discovered them through the reward structure, the same way DQN/PPO/MADDPG discovered coordination strategies in the drone project this extends.

The RAG faithfulness checker correctly scores fabricated statistics at 0.0 and accurately-grounded reports at 1.0 in testing (see `eval/faithfulness.py` docstring and inline tests).

## Design decisions worth knowing for an interview

- **Why derive team stats from raw games instead of using a stats endpoint?** The free API tier doesn't expose season averages/standings (paid-tier only) — so this project builds its own analytics layer from raw scores. This ended up being a better engineering demonstration than calling a pre-built endpoint would have been.
- **Why TF-IDF instead of neural embeddings for retrieval?** The corpus is small (30 short, keyword-heavy structured documents). A large embedding model would add latency and complexity for no real retrieval-quality gain at this scale — matching the tool to the problem, not defaulting to the fanciest option.
- **Why tabular Q-learning instead of deep RL?** The clutch-possession state space is small and fully enumerable (5 score buckets × ~9 possession-count values). A neural network would be solving a ~180-cell lookup table with an oversized hammer — same judgment call as choosing DQN vs. PPO vs. MADDPG per-scenario in the drone project.
- **Why a deterministic faithfulness checker instead of an LLM judge?** For structured numeric claims, exact-match-with-tolerance is cheaper, faster, and more reliable than asking another model to eyeball faithfulness.

## Honest limitations (worth stating up front, not hiding)

- The RL environment's shot-success rates are *estimated* from scoring efficiency, since the free API tier doesn't expose shot-location/type data. This is a documented modeling simplification, not a claim of measured shot-selection data.
- The faithfulness checker validates *numeric* grounding; it doesn't yet check the semantic correctness of qualitative claims (e.g., "trending hot" framing).
- Retrieval is exact-match/TF-IDF, appropriate for this small structured corpus, but wouldn't scale as-is to a much larger free-text corpus (e.g., full play-by-play or news articles) — a neural embedding retriever would be the natural next step there.

## Possible extensions

- Add a small multi-agent layer: model the opponent as a learning agent too (closer to the MADDPG formulation from the drone project) rather than a fixed skill profile
- Swap in an embedding-based retriever if the corpus grows to include free-text scouting articles/injury reports
- Add play-by-play data (available from the 2025 season onward) to replace the estimated shot-success rates with measured ones
